newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank to convert state interest payments.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank to convert state interest payments.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank said on Monday it had decided to convert government interest payments into foreign currencies in the banking system in its capacity as the National Debt Office's foreign exchange agent.
"In 1997 it is estimated that the National Debt Office will be paying out the equivalent of about 20 billion crowns in interest on foreign currency liabilities," the central bank said in a statement.
"In periods when the office's net borrowing in foreign currency exceeded such interest payments, the loans could be used to make the foreign currency interest payments," it said.
The Riksbank decided in November it would no longer be a net borrower in foreign currency.
"As a consequence of that decision the Riksbank, acting as the office's agent, will be converting the interest payments in the banking system," the Riksbank said.
It said it would keep transactions down to 80 million crowns per day between 0830 and 0845 local time (0730-0745 GMT).

"In order to avoid unduly large exchange transactions, the equivalent of 80 million crowns will be exchanged on each trading day during 1997, which gives an annual total of about 20 billion crowns," it said.
"The Riksbank intends to begin these transactions in January 1997."
The transactions will be arranged with the Riksbank's primary dealers for the Swedish foreign exchange market.
"The Riksbank intends these transactions to be completely open," the central bank said.
